note: Help > About in TBC. Two minutes, and every question about TBC behaviour below is conditional on the answer.
Walk out to the vehicle. Is a GAMS antenna pair fitted, is a DMI on a non-steering wheel, which rack. Settles five Preflight items and the whole GAMS/DMI branch of trajectory processing.
Ask IT whether a POSPac MMS 8.6+ licence exists and where it is installed. D-19, T10 and V-9 all assume an answer.
Open TMI and read the screen. The Preflight asks the operator which presentation they saw; this says which one they will see.
The TMI device list names the cameras actually present. Same look as T27.
The TMI device list, then the TBC export dialog. Answers V-8 at the same time.
Open Register a Mission and read the Auto-Saving checkbox state. One look.
Ask whoever fitted the DMI whether the wheel was measured. If it was not, the 5 percent default stands and should be recorded as such.
Name the owner and the review cycle, one line, into SOP Appendix C. Costs nothing, and nothing in this set can be adopted until somebody owns it.
Who may operate, register, accept a registration, run Cleanup, sign an accuracy statement, own calibration currency. One table. D-15, D-29, D-35 and D-36 all wait on it.
Fix the control/check designation before registration and forbid changing it during. The Office How To already says so; this makes it binding.
Datum and epoch, who sets them, who checks them. Written once, applies to every project.
Largely written already: Appendix B and the Field Record Form are the content. This adopts them.
Transfer, verification and backup. The Field How To already describes it; this makes it the procedure.
Folder structure and naming. The Field Tools record ids already assume a project and a task; this is where those records land.

Adopt Trimble's documented initialization, closing and control-bracketing sequences as Parametrix requirements, or keep them as recommended practice. One meeting, and it turns 'should' into 'shall' across the Field How To.
When Cleanup may be run and what must be archived first. The Archive and Cleanup checklist is already the sequence; this makes it binding.
The corridor continuity inspection method and coverage. QC layer 6 is written; this fixes what it covers.
What is verified at import and by whom. The Office Processing checklist already lists the checks.
Whether LiDAR QC is a capability we intend to have. T13 and V-9 only matter if it is.
Whether scans are generated coloured by default.
Whether the imagery file-size scan is adopted as a QC step.
Whether a chain-of-custody record is required. The Field Tools record already carries most of one.
Base station strategy and maximum baseline. Means nothing until the trajectory method is chosen.
IN-Fusion+ Single Base or PP-RTX. Needs the licence question answered first.
Where lever arms, the Vehicle Preset and the installation configuration are recorded and verified.
The corridor default registration command. Decide once the registration-type test has been run.
Whether the retro-reflective target check is our periodic verification, and at what interval.
Recalibration interval and triggers, and what happens to data collected on a stale calibration. Waits on Trimble saying whether refitting the Sensor Unit disturbs it.
Where the calibration site is and who maintains it. D-26 is hollow without it.
What a visual point-cloud QC pass and an imagery QC pass cover.
The record package: what accompanies a deliverable and where it lives.
The decision rule when a corridor produces an unacceptable trajectory, and whether marginal segments are delivered.
Standard deliverable formats, which export path produces each, and default scaling.
Field operating rules: wet-weather go/no-go with operator stand-down authority, night collection, speed by deliverable type, free-space margin.
Retention: what is kept, where, for how long, by whom. Overlaps the imagery privacy question.
Imagery privacy, and whether unblurred originals are retained. A policy and legal question, not a technical one; it needs whoever owns records retention.
The export release gate, and whether exports may be made with Export timestamps enabled.
Passes and pattern by roadway type. Informed by the overlap test.
Whether airfield pavement roughness is a service Parametrix offers, and on what validation scheme.
The acceptance criteria. Nothing may be quoted to a client until this exists, and it should not be written before the registration and control tests give it numbers.
Control design: how many points, at what spacing, how many independent checks. With D-13, the pair that blocks delivering for a stated accuracy purpose.
On a scratch copy of a project, never a live one, because the command cannot be undone.
Needs one generated run with signs and line marking in it.
Which Parametrix coordinate systems POSPac recognises directly.
Only worth running if LiDAR QC is a capability we intend to have.
Working cutting plane thickness for the visual checks. Feeds D-27.
Whether Sample points really thins at random in the classified LAS exporter.
Register a mission, run a Mission Report, look for the signed GCP residuals. Answers V-11 at the same time.
Export a LAS and read the header, the VLRs and the sidecar. Answers V-12 by inspection, which is faster than asking.
Draw a Point Cloud tab selection across two trajectories and watch what happens.
Whether exported imagery reflects a registration adjustment.
Forward versus backward camera preference in the colouriser, and its effect on fringing.
Filter selection and defaults: Default against High Quality, Isolated Points, Range Max, Fog and Sun.
Target-Bundle Adjustment, both states, with independent checks.
Whether Multipath Medium is right for open-sky corridors.
Export the same registered run twice, timestamps off and on, and compare geometry. Blocks the export release gate.
Publish a registered run to TRCPS and export it to TMX, and inspect what arrives.
Establish the reliable export-state verification method for each export path.
Both provenance reconstruction paths, on a dataset with two candidate trajectories.
Global, Local and Global-then-Local with independent checks. The test D-12 and D-13 both wait on, and the single most valuable day at the workstation.
The TBC Boeing Bump Index report end to end on an MX60 dataset. Blocks D-57 and the airfield offer.
The six TBC mobile mapping commands this document set does not cover.
Which feature types are fit for horizontal control, vertical control or both. Needs a control survey beside an MX60 pass.
How much run overlap is enough for run-to-run registration. Needs a deliberate overlapping pass.
Whether a predicted GNSS environment correlates with achieved trajectory RMS. The expensive one; run it alongside real work rather than on its own.
Confirm the configuration from the serial number in writing. D-2 can be settled by looking, but this is the record of it.
A straight conflict between two Trimble documents on the scanner field of view. The conflict ledger already records it; Trimble has to say which is right.
Request the GAMS Antenna Kit and DMI Installation manuals from the dealer. Neither is held.
Does removing and refitting the Sensor Unit disturb the calibration, and what shows drift. Blocks the recalibration interval.
When Export timestamps causes reprocessing from raw, which trajectory is used.
Which trajectory TMX export and Publish to TRCPS send when a run has both.
Whether any TBC export writes the source trajectory into a LAS header, VLR or sidecar. T22 may answer it first.
Whether the retro-reflective target check is the recommended periodic verification, and at what interval. Blocks D-28.
Whether LiDAR QC has its own POSPac dependency.
Which report contains the signed GCP residuals. Ask only if the Mission Report test does not find them.
When PFIX should be preferred over registration.
Whether the coordinate-system-without-Geoid restriction on TMX export applies to the MX60 or only the MX9.
Whether the Lateral Range Limit affects accuracy or is purely a data-volume tool.
Whether the 30-minute minimum mission time is enforced by TMI, and why it exists.
